name: Rhetorical Device & Persuasive Pattern Analysis
description: Analyzes the text for the organic integration of rhetorical devices such as parallelism, chiasmus, rhetorical questions, and deliberate hyperbole. Human writers use these devices intuitively to persuade, emphasize, or create a distinct voice. Large Language Models generally produce highly literal, flat, and objective prose. When AI attempts to use rhetorical devices (usually due to a specific prompt like 'write persuasively'), the execution is often formulaic, heavily clichéd, or structurally over-indexed (e.g., using exactly three parallel points every time).
algorithm: Stylistic Tropes and Schematic Pattern Recognition
mechanism: The algorithm detects deviations from standard literal syntax that indicate rhetorical structuring. It specifically looks for 'schemes' (patterns of words like parallelism/anaphora) and 'tropes' (figures of speech like metaphors/irony). The system calculates a 'Rhetorical Authenticity Score' by looking at the density, distribution, and structural predictability of these devices. A human speech writer might use a complex chiasmus organically. An AI model typically relies on basic, predictable rhetorical questions ('But what does this mean for the future?') or rigid tricolon structures ('Safe, secure, and reliable').
useCase: Highly effective for auditing opinion pieces, political speeches, marketing copy, and persuasive essays where distinguishing between genuine human passion and forced AI 'persuasiveness' is critical.
strengths:
• Exceptional at detecting AI that has been explicitly prompted to 'write like a human blogger' or 'make it sound exciting.'
• Captures higher-order stylistic intent that goes beyond simple vocabulary or grammar checks.
limitations:
• Prone to false positives on extremely poor human writing that relies on clichés and basic rhetorical tropes.
• Not useful for analyzing purely informational texts (e.g., lab reports, technical documentation) where rhetorical devices are naturally absent.
parameters:
Analysis: Syntactic Scheme and Trope Detection
Metric: Rhetorical Predictability and Cliché Density
Output: 0-100 Stylistic Artificiality (Forced Rhetoric) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 72-80% accuracy. Achieves optimal forensic results when paired with Emotional Formality and Register Variation.
